question: Why are deep yellow and orange vegetables so good for your health?

options.A: It speeds up the absorption of glucose in the gut
options.B: It binds directly to cholesterol in the stomach
options.C: It acts as a precursor to vitamin A in the body
options.D: It serves as the main structural protein for cell walls

explanation: Great job! Beta-carotene is simply a plant pigment that your body turns into vitamin A, which keeps your eyes and immune system strong.

question: How does fiber from vegetables help keep your blood sugar steady?

options.A: By slowing down the rate at which glucose is absorbed in the gut
options.B: By directly destroying excess sugar molecules in the bloodstream
options.C: By converting surplus glucose into stored body fat for later use
options.D: By stimulating the pancreas to produce more insulin immediately

explanation: You've got this! Fiber slows down digestion, which stops sugar from rushing into your blood all at once and causing sudden spikes.

question: Which group of vegetables is famous for helping your liver clear out toxins?
explanation: Spot on! Vegetables like cabbage and broccoli belong to the cruciferous family and contain special compounds that give your liver a helping hand.

question: A patient asks which vegetable group is packed with vitamin C and lycopene. What's your best reply?

options.A: Leafy greens like spinach and pumpkin leaves
options.B: Bulb vegetables like onions and garlic
options.C: Fruiting vegetables like tomatoes and peppers
options.D: Root vegetables like carrots and beets

explanation: Exactly! Tomatoes, peppers, and garden eggs grow from the flowering parts of plants and are loaded with vitamin C and antioxidants.

question: What is the daily amount of vegetables recommended to help adults stay healthy?

options.A: About 400 grams or roughly five servings
options.B: At least 1 kilogram divided into ten meals
options.C: Only 50 grams taken once a week
options.D: Exactly 100 grams or one large serving

explanation: Well done! Health guidelines generally suggest aiming for around 400 grams of fruits and veggies daily to keep chronic illnesses at bay.

question: Why do pregnant women need to eat plenty of dark green leafy vegetables?

options.A: They supply essential folate and iron needed for fetal neural development and blood volume
options.B: They completely eliminate morning sickness by neutralizing stomach acid
options.C: They replace the need for all routine prenatal vitamin supplements
options.D: They prevent the mother from gaining any excess weight during the pregnancy

explanation: You're doing great! Dark greens give moms-to-be iron for extra blood and folate to protect the baby's developing brain and spine.

question: Which popular Nigerian vegetable is well-known as a fantastic plant source of iron?
explanation: Correct! Ugu is a local favorite that packs a serious iron punch, making it brilliant for fighting off anemia.

question: Why do cooks love adding waterleaf to traditional Nigerian soups and stews?

options.A: It turns the broth into a solid gel when allowed to cool down
options.B: It serves as a strong preservative to keep soups from spoiling quickly
options.C: It acts as a natural thickening agent while adding moisture and vitamins
options.D: It completely replaces the need for adding palm oil to the pot

explanation: Spot on! Waterleaf breaks down nicely during cooking to give soups a rich texture while boosting the vitamin content.

question: Which vitamins are most easily lost when vegetables are boiled in too much water?

options.A: Inert plant fibers like cellulose and lignin
options.B: Water-soluble vitamins like vitamin C and B vitamins
options.C: Fat-soluble vitamins like vitamin A and vitamin E
options.D: Structural minerals like calcium and iron

explanation: You got it! Vitamins C and B love water, so they dissolve right out of the veggies and into the cooking pot.

question: Why is it smart not to throw away the broth after boiling vegetables?

options.A: It slows down digestion so much that hunger never returns
options.B: It neutralizes all harmful bacteria that may have survived the cooking process
options.C: It recaptures water-soluble vitamins and minerals that leaked out during boiling
options.D: It provides all the dietary protein required for the day in one serving

explanation: Brilliant! Drinking the soup broth ensures you don't lose all those valuable vitamins that leaked out into the water.

question: What is a simple, practical way to store extra green vegetables when electricity is unreliable?

options.A: Sealing in airtight glass jars with heavy salt

explanation: Correct! Sun-drying and blanching are time-tested ways to keep your veggies from spoiling without needing a fridge.

question: Why is buying vegetables that are currently "in season" a smart strategy?

options.A: It ensures the vegetables have zero water content inside them
options.B: It guarantees that the vegetables will never contain any natural toxins
options.C: It makes fresh produce more affordable and readily available in the local market
options.D: It eliminates the need to wash the produce before cooking it

explanation: Well reasoned! When crops are in season, they are abundant and cheap, making healthy eating much easier on the wallet.

question: What is the best approach when a nurse gives dietary advice to a patient with a chronic condition?

options.A: Telling the patient to rely entirely on vitamin supplements instead of food
options.B: Focusing solely on what foods the patient must completely ban from the house
options.C: Tailoring advice to fit the patient's cultural background, finances, and lifestyle
options.D: Handing out a strict, pre-printed meal plan that cannot be changed

explanation: Spot on! Advice only works if it fits into the patient's real life, budget, and cultural preferences.

question: A patient with type 2 diabetes needs help managing their meals. What is a great, simple tip to share first?

options.A: Replace all water intake with fresh vegetable juices only
options.B: Cook your vegetables without any seasoning or oil whatsoever
options.C: Stop eating all forms of food for two days of the week
options.D: Fill half of your meal plate with non-starchy, colorful vegetables

explanation: You nailed it! The plate method is a fantastic, visual way to help patients control portions and get enough fiber without stressful calorie counting.
